first.rationale: I intend to test a shorter, simpler onboarding flow because onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence links onboarding improvements to faster time-to-value. I will verify the onboarding and activation records before committing. The experiment should measure qualified revenue and retention, not just completion, to ensure increased activation does not reduce downstream value.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The current decline in onboarding completion is the most direct problem, and verified evidence shows shortened onboarding improves completion, reduces time-to-value, and increases 30-day retention. It should also support activation recovery, while avoiding the retention risk associated with promotional pricing. Measure completion, activation, time-to-value, qualified revenue, and 30-day retention before broad rollout.

final2.rationale: Keep the committed onboarding experiment for this cycle rather than switching to promotional pricing. The deeper competitor cut raises urgency, but existing evidence shows promotional pricing materially harms 30-day retention, conflicting with sustainable qualified revenue. Simplified onboarding has verified positive effects on completion, time-to-value, and retention, while its impact on price-driven churn remains uncertain. Track price-sensitive SMB churn and qualified revenue as guardrails, and revisit targeted commercial responses next cycle.
